correctness.rationale: The two defining powers force m x^(m-1) f = n y^(n-1) f = 0, and these conditions suffice for the weighted determinant bracket on polynomial representatives to descend. An alternating biderivation has an alternating Jacobiator which is a derivation in each argument: expansion by Leibniz cancels the cross terms in pairs, also in characteristic two. Its generator triples therefore vanish, proving Jacobi on the quotient. For f=f0 g with f0=x^a y^b, the centre kernel contains the f0 kernel and agrees with it whenever g is a unit. This gives the claimed minimum over every field and the stated coordinate open and finite-field population, without identifying that open with the full minimum stratum. For each derivative separately the nonzero shifted monomial images have distinct exponents. Intersecting the two kernel masks and grouping by whether the exponents are divisible by p gives the four terms in the dimension formula (in characteristic zero use exponent zero). The values on x and y of the two-coordinate centrality map are independent for nonzero f; for the socle weight exactly those two monomials survive. A unit weight is possible precisely when both defining powers have zero formal derivative, and then the common derivative kernel is k[x^p,y^p].
residual_risks: The bundled finite checker enumerates inside the predicted parameter ideal and tests Jacobi only on selected weights; it is not independent proof of admissibility or of arbitrary-field Jacobi. The proof supplies both.

value.rationale: The centre is degree-zero Poisson cohomology. Knowing its explicit generic basis and sharp extrema across a natural family of singular algebras identifies exactly how modular derivative zeros and truncation interact, including asymmetric cases not present in the standard complex and symplectic examples. The count refers to a concrete open set rather than claiming a full stratification.
residual_risks: No classification of isomorphism orbits, higher cohomology or all nongeneric strata follows.
